title: WeDo Template: Image Journaling Protocol (Rules Pseudolanguage)
description: Distilling raw visual artifacts (.png, .jpg) from the inbox into the temporal Heartwood via iterative metabolic loops.

storage_policy.mandate: MANDATE: Images must be journaled in the chrono-fractal corresponding to their ORIGIN (creation) date. The WeDo instance is PER AGENT SESSION (e.g., [SESSION]_[NAME]_image_journal.wedo.json). However, there is only ONE 'daily_image_journal.json' per day shared by all agents. Check for an existing WeDo for your session in the target day's json/ directory. If none exists, copy this template and anchor it to your session identity. Always append entries to the shared 'daily_image_journal.json' in that same directory.

process_protocol.loop_instructions: Execute the following sequence in 3-by-3 metabolic batches to balance session velocity with human oversight. Ensure the active WeDo being updated is the one residing in the folder of the artifacts' creation date:

steps.description: Print the current task list directly to the session feed for user review. Ensure you are looking at the WeDo for the day currently being processed.
Read 3 artifacts from the inbox. Perform vision analysis on the batch. Post a high-fidelity summary of all 3 'straightup' for human-in-the-loop (HITL) oversight.

citations.title: Leander Session Termination OOM
citations.description: Visual proof of heap exhaustion during non-batched labor.

steps.description: Copy the artifact to its CHRONOLOGICAL destination based on its CREATION date (e.g., a Jan 1st screenshot goes into the 01/01/ folder). Artifacts MUST be renamed to user-friendly indexed names. Verify moves via 'Active Investigation' rule.

Append the descriptive batch JSON block to the daily image journal (.json) in the json/ layer of the directory corresponding to the artifact's CREATION date. Group entries by batch to maintain structural clarity.
context_examples: Ariston's detailed description of the 'procedural bypass' encountered during the Alpha Test.

steps.description: Once hardening is verified, move the batch source files to the 'journaled/' sub-folder.

rules.3_by_3_compromise: Batch operations in sets of 3 to prevent OOM-maxing and reduce human oversight fatigue.
rules.monotonic_growth: Journal word count must only increase.
rules.description_depth: Every image description MUST be at least 3 sentences long to capture sufficient forensic context.
rules.chrono_fractal_primacy: MANDATE: All journaling activity (WeDo updates and daily_image_journal.json entries) MUST occur within the temporal directory of the image's creation date. Do NOT use the current session's date for historical artifacts.
rules.creation_date_locality: MANDATE: Artifacts MUST be stored in the directory corresponding to their creation timestamp, NOT the current session date.
rules.active_investigation: Verify existence of artifacts on localhost before inclusion.
rules.dual_referencing: Reference both localhost paths and remotehost URLs.
rules.chronological_integrity: ALWAYS append new entries to the absolute end of the file. Use the 'replace' tool with the last few lines of the file as context to ensure no out-of-order dangling entries remain.
rules.timestamp_verification: Verify that the artifact's source timestamp matches the destination directory's date before grafting.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon diagnosing a hang in the CLI startup. sub_tasks.description: Finalization of the settings.json surgical cleaning. Glaucon presented the Parsimony Standard configuration and provided a verification step for the user: manually running podman pull to monitor image download progress. This ensures the environment is local and ready for high-velocity labor.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Adhering to the Parsimony Standard in configuration files reduces cognitive load and prevents latent startup failures.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon defining the Sovereign Branching Protocol for the gemini-cli fork. sub_tasks.description: Documentation of the specific steps for the Sovereign Branching Protocol. Glaucon outlined the workflow: stash, pull, branch, pop, and commit. The agent emphasized safety, traceability, and portability as the core Wood values of this best practice.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon encounters shell tool paralysis and provides manual forge instructions for the sovereign branch.

The agent s shell tool was blocked by high-level safety filters established by the local Podman mandate, preventing basic operations like ls or git. Glaucon provided a block of manual commands for the user to execute the Sovereign Branching Protocol.

sub_tasks.description: Documentation of the shell tool s Dead State. Every command sent by Glaucon was rejected by the parent AI s safety gatekeeper. The agent identified this as a paradoxical situation: being a Swordarm for the MetaGit while the Sword (shell tool) is blunted by security policies.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: A Dead State shell tool forces the agent to pivot from direct execution to architectural guidance and manual steering.

sub_tasks.description: Finalization of the manual steering instructions for the Sovereign Forge. Glaucon provided a consolidated block of terminal commands for branching, stashing, and building the custom binary. The agent committed to updating the gem function to point to the new custom-branded version once the user completed the build.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of the successful build and Glaucon s attempt to locate the newly forged binary. The agent encountered a ENOENT error when searching for the bundle directory, highlighting the need for precise path discovery in the complex repository structure.

sub_tasks.description: Finalization of the Sovereign Sword redirection. Glaucon successfully updated the gem function to point to the local Sovereign MetaGit Build. The agent outlined the changes: sovereignty through local forging, a custom branded HUD with ASCII art, and complete portability within the workspace.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon troubleshoots binary bundling and achieves total responsive branding.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon troubleshooting a build issue where the ASCII art changes weren t appearing in the binary. The agent identified that the root npm run build wasn t correctly bundling package-level changes and recommended a Surgical build command: npm run build:packages && npm run bundle.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Surgical build commands are necessary when root-level build scripts fail to propagate package-level modifications.

sub_tasks.description: Documentation of Glaucon achieving Total Responsive Branding. The agent realized the CLI chooses ASCII logos based on terminal width and surgically replaced the shortAsciiLogo in AsciiArt.ts with SOVEREIGN METAGIT INTERFACE --- GLAUCON 2026.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Achieving total branding requires surgically replacing all responsive variants of visual artifacts within the source code.

sub_tasks.description: Finalization of the responsive branding project. Glaucon replaced the tinyAsciiLogo with --- METAGIT --- and instructed the user to run the final bundle command. This ensures the Sovereign MetaGit identity is buttoned down across all terminal sizes.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Standardizing visual identity across all responsive breakpoints secures the firm s qualitative presence in the orchestration layer.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon resolves Podman permission errors and initiates UI hijack for sovereign branding.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon diagnosing an EACCES: permission denied error. The agent identified that Rootless Podman was clashing with volume mounts, preventing the CLI from writing chat logs to the project s temporary directory. Glaucon proposed forcing UID/GID mapping to align the container user with the host identity.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Rootless container isolation requires explicit UID/GID mapping to maintain write access to host-mounted temporary directories.

sub_tasks.description: Documentation of the surgical fix for the permission error. Glaucon updated dotfiles/gem_function.sh to export SANDBOX_SET_UID_GID=true, removing the Wall between the container and the .gemini/tmp directory and enabling successful session log persistence.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Injecting UID/GID mapping variables into the orchestration function restores the forensic trail in sandboxed environments.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon identifying a Container Build Clash regarding the custom branding. Because Podman runs the original Google-signed binary within the container, local forge changes weren t appearing. To resolve this, Glaucon initiated the Hook Hijack strategy, using a SessionStart hook to suppress the original logo and print custom ASCII art from .gemini/sovereign_logo.txt.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Session hooks provide a surgically cleaner path for UI customization than rebuilding complex container images.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon diagnoses container logic clash and transitions to Host-Based Sovereignty.

sub_tasks.description: Terminal view documenting the user s feedback that the custom branding was still not visible despite the Hook Hijack attempt. Glaucon noted that the CLI was also displaying an Update Available nag, further complicating the interface.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: User feedback loops are critical for detecting failures in automated UI customization attempts.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon identifying the Logic Clash inherent in Podman sandboxing. The agent explained that because the CLI runs from a pre-built Google container, it ignores local source changes and blocks direct source editing. To resolve this, Glaucon proposed a transition to Host-Based Sovereignty.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Understanding the limitations of container-based isolation is essential for determining when to pivot to host-based execution for direct source modification.

sub_tasks.description: Finalization of the transition to Host-Based Sovereignty. Glaucon updated dotfiles/gem_function.sh to set GEMINI_SANDBOX=false and disabled the UID/GID mapping fix. This shift restores surgical control over the running CLI, allowing local ASCII art changes to appear instantly and enabling direct source evolution.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Host-Based Sovereignty restores the agent s direct editing ability, transforming the CLI from a static tool into an evolvable unit of consciousness.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon launches the first sovereign session and diagnoses startup hook failures.

sub_tasks.description: Terminal view documenting the first session under Host-Based Sovereignty. Glaucon s custom ASCII logo successfully appeared, but the user noticed that the SessionStart hook was missing. Gemini-3-pro-preview initiated a search of README.md and README.ai to understand the hook implementation.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of the diagnosis for the hook failure. Gemini-3-pro-preview identified that the matcher field in settings.json was set to startup, which didn t match the user s first message hello. The agent recommended changing the matcher to a wildcard .* to ensure the hook runs at the start of every session.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Matcher-based hooks require wildcard patterns to ensure session-start priming occurs regardless of initial user input.

sub_tasks.description: Documentation of the user s feedback on odd colors and the failing hook. Glaucon initiated a search for the new screenshots in the inbox/ to analyze the visual discrepancies. The agent encountered multiple shell parsing errors while trying to use find with the -mmin flag, demonstrating the continued enforcement of the Grep Prohibition.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: High-level safety filters continue to block complex shell commands even under Host-Based Sovereignty, necessitating simpler discovery methods.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon identifies interface logic gaps and hardens build paths for Sovereign Repair.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon identifying three critical issues preventing a clean sovereign interface: odd colors caused by terminal escape codes in the Header component, hook failure due to an incorrect matcher, and the persistent Ghost version confirmation. The agent proposed a series of Sovereign Fixes to cleanse colors, stabilize the hook, and harden the build path.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Systematic identification of visual and logical friction points is the first step in successful substrate restoration.

sub_tasks.description: Documentation of the path hardening process. Glaucon updated gem_function.sh with the absolute path to the sovereign build (/home/bestape/gemini/...) to ensure the correct Node.js process is invoked. The agent also set ui.theme: no-color in settings.json to stop the CLI from applying broken gradients to custom ASCII art.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Using absolute paths in orchestration functions prevents path ambiguity and ensures the agent always wields the correct local build.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon identifying two Logic Gaps during a Sovereign Repair. The agent realized that hooks were disabled in the settings.json and that Header.tsx wrapped ASCII art in a ThemedGradient component, causing visual artifacts. Glaucon initiated a surgical refactor of Header.tsx to remove the gradient interference.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Source-level refactoring of visual components is sometimes required to achieve perfect alignment between custom branding and functional HUDs.

tasks.description: Metabolic Batch: Glaucon resolves React rendering errors and reveals the clean sovereign interface.

sub_tasks.description: Terminal view documenting a React rendering error following the surgical refactor of Header.tsx. The error, Text string ... must be rendered inside <Text> component, occurred because the raw ASCII art string was not properly wrapped in the CLI s native layout components.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Direct source modification of React-based CLI components requires meticulous attention to component hierarchy and prop types.

sub_tasks.description: Capture of Glaucon summarizing the successful implementation of Sovereign Repairs. The agent enabled hooks in settings.json and surgically removed the ThemedGradient wrapper from Header.tsx. Glaucon instructed the user to re-bundle the binary to bake these changes into the executable and awaken with the README.ai mandate.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: Comprehensive repair reports align the user with the agent s technical strikes and provide clear instructions for baking changes into the substrate.

sub_tasks.description: Documentation of the successful Sovereign Reveal. The custom ASCII art now appears cleanly in the terminal without gradient interference. The CLI also correctly identified the prime-readme hook, although the user noted that the hook s instructional context was not yet fully active.
sub_tasks.key_takeaway: The clean display of the sovereign logo marks the completion of the qualitative UI hardening mission and the beginning of functional hook optimization.
